data.name: Erminie
data.gender_notes: Erminie is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Erminie is derived from the Latin word ‘erminus’, meaning ‘ermine’ or ‘pure one’. In ancient times, the ermine was a symbol of purity and grace. This name was also given to girls who were born during the winter months, as the ermine's white fur was a reminder of the snow. The name Erminie carries the meaning “Ermine, the pure one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Erminie usually hope their child will grow to embody ermine, the pure one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Erminie total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Erminie has a rich cultural history, particularly in France. It was popularized during the Middle Ages when the ermine was a common symbol in heraldry. Many noble families used the ermine in their coats of arms, and the name became associated with nobility, purity, and grace.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, the name Erminie carries the meaning of purity and innocence. It is a reminder to live a life that is clean and untarnished, just like the pristine white fur of the ermine. Additionally, the name Erminie can be seen as a reflection of the men and women of faith, striving to live in a manner that is pleasing to God and reflects the purity and grace of His divine nature.
